summary: Obfuscated browser loader that fetches and eval()s remote JavaScript
details: The package ships a single heavily obfuscated file (a140ulh5.js) with a stub package.json that declares no main/bin/scripts/files fields. The file uses obfuscator.io string-array rotation with a custom base64 decoder and embeds two ~10KB opaque base64 blobs that are decoded via atob() and executed with new Function(). On load (when document is defined), it auto-bootstraps, installs a globalThis[Symbol.for(...)] handle, and fetches JS text from a configured base URL which it then executes via new Function(responseText)(). Any site that bundles or references this file exposes its end users to arbitrary remote code execution controlled by whoever operates the loader's base URL, with no source-available counterpart and no integrity check on the fetched payload. The obfuscation, embedded opaque executables, and absence of any declared package entrypoint are consistent with a covert code-delivery channel rather than a legitimate CDN loader.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
